video_title: Stewie & Myles on Team USA, Mamba Mentality & Leaving a Legacy

quotes.speaker: Breanna Stewart
quotes.summary_phrase: The unique challenge of FIBA Women's World Cup preparation
quotes.excerpt: The crazy part is we have no time. We're heading out on Sunday, some people are leaving on Monday.

text_blocks.speaker: Myles Turner
text_blocks.text: The World Cup is the time to shine and where you can genuinely bring so much joy and energy back to your country. What's it like when the group first meets up? In your case, take time away from the season to come for a collective goal.

text_blocks.speaker: Breanna Stewart
text_blocks.text: The crazy part is we have no time. I'm heading out on Sunday, some people are leaving on Monday, which means games start on Friday. There is two days of practice and then games. Once we get there, we are literally locked in, got to get into it and know that we have to all be on the same page.

quotes.speaker: Myles Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: The shift from tryouts to selection in international basketball
quotes.excerpt: It used to be that way with the men's Olympics, but now they just pick.

text_blocks.speaker: Myles Turner
text_blocks.text: We had a tryout for the team. There was no we pick you, we pick you, we pick you. They invited 30 of us and we had a tryout and actually make the team. It used to be that way with the men's Olympics, but now they just pick, which has its advantages and disadvantages.

text_blocks.speaker: Breanna Stewart
text_blocks.text: I don't think it takes much time. The respect thing is so high, you respect everybody that you're going to share the court with. The moment that you do get there, you're excited about it.

quotes.speaker: Breanna Stewart
quotes.summary_phrase: The fundamental differences between FIBA and NBA basketball rules
quotes.excerpt: You cannot open step. You cannot rip and go. If you rip and go, it's a travel.

text_blocks.speaker: Breanna Stewart
text_blocks.text: The biggest thing is you cannot open step. You cannot rip and go. If you rip and go, it's a travel. You have to really change your footing, you have to drop the ball early. That's my biggest adjustment.

text_blocks.speaker: Myles Turner
text_blocks.text: It's like old school NBA. You weren't going to run through the lane without getting an elbow to the throat or an elbow to the chin. It's a physical game and a lot of people refuse to go inside because there's no defensive three seconds.

quotes.speaker: Breanna Stewart
quotes.summary_phrase: Breanna Stewart's reliance on experience for Team USA
quotes.excerpt: This will be my fourth World Cup, which I am definitely really proud of.
quotes.quote: What I am going to be most relied on for is obviously my experience. This will be my fourth World Cup, which I am definitely really proud of, to be able to just continue to show up every four years, no matter what it is. But also the versatility, the ability to play three-four, to switch a lot if we need to depending on team-by-team basis, and going in there with an open mind, but obviously very confident and knowing that we got to go get it done.

quotes.speaker: Breanna Stewart
quotes.summary_phrase: The 'Mamba Mentality' required for international competition
quotes.excerpt: When you're representing your country, you're full on Mamba mentality.

text_blocks.speaker: Myles Turner
text_blocks.text: Is it that friendly competition thing or full on Mamba mentality like I'm here to fuck shit up?

text_blocks.speaker: Breanna Stewart
text_blocks.text: When you're representing your country, you're full on Mamba mentality. I can be off cool with my teammates before the game, but once that ball goes up, we have to get after it. Game one, we start with China, so it's me versus Han Xu, which will be really cool.

quotes.speaker: Myles Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Myles Turner on Kobe Bryant's intensity during international play
quotes.excerpt: Kobe Bryant and Pau Gasol were teammates with the Lakers, and the USA was playing Spain.
quotes.quote: There's a viral clip, it's hilarious to me when this happened, but Kobe Bryant and Pau Gasol were teammates with the Lakers, and the USA was playing Spain in the Olympics. Kobe had said before the game the very first thing he would do is run through Pau's chest. Sure enough, he did just that. There was a loose ball and Kobe ran full speed into Pau Gasol and knocked him on his ass and didn't say shit to him. That's the mentality you have to bring into this international game.

quotes.speaker: Myles Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Why Victor Wembanyama is the face of the NBA
quotes.excerpt: The first person that pops in my head is obviously Wembanyama.
quotes.quote: The first person that pops in my head is obviously Wembanyama. The reason I say this is not just because of his basketball talent, it's because the way he represents himself, the things he does off the floor, the person that he becomes. As an NBA representative, you have to be a humanitarian. You have to be someone that is highly marketable, someone that is recognizable, but also someone that doesn't have much drama off the floor. Wembanyama has done an amazing job of keeping his family first.

quotes.speaker: Breanna Stewart
quotes.summary_phrase: The WNBA's expansion and growth trajectory
quotes.excerpt: The biggest change is definitely going to be more games. You're going to see that next year.
quotes.quote: The biggest change is definitely going to be more games. You're going to see that next year. We're going to go from 44 to 50. Even this year, we have a seven-game playoff series, which is kind of crazy. But it's exciting. More games means the season is going to be longer, it's going to be more spread out, so you can actually get good quality basketball.

quotes.speaker: Myles Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: How playoff scouting changes for individual players
quotes.excerpt: Anytime he puts his hands on his knees, the ball is coming to him.
quotes.quote: One thing I thought was so funny in the playoffs two years ago, we were playing Jalen Brunson, and the scout literally said anytime he puts his hands on his knees, the ball is coming to him. Anytime he puts his hands on his knees, the ball came to him every time. It's like a weird basketball psychology thing, you're trying to psych people out like you're not involved in the play. He did it every single time.

quotes.speaker: Breanna Stewart
quotes.summary_phrase: Why the best player doesn't always take the last shot
quotes.excerpt: I don't think that the best player always has to take the last shot.
quotes.quote: I don't think that the best player always has to take the last shot because it's dependent on what you need. But they're going to be in the action, because gravitational pull. More likely than not, you know the ball is coming to certain people.

quotes.speaker: Myles Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Using star players as decoys in late-game situations
quotes.excerpt: Everyone in the gym knows the ball is going to Stephen Curry, so use that to your advantage.
quotes.quote: Coaches play games at times. Everyone in the gym knows the ball is going to Stephen Curry, so use that to your advantage. You can almost use him as a decoy and all the attention is on him. Now all of a sudden you got someone wide open in the corner who is a career 45% three-point shooter, and boom, knocks it in. They don't necessarily always have to take the last shot, but they always do need to be a focal point.

quotes.speaker: Myles Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Myles Turner on managing social media negativity
quotes.excerpt: I never tune into the TV part of things, the ESPN, the SportsCenter, the first take.
quotes.quote: The one thing I make sure I never do is I never tune into the TV part of things, the ESPN, the SportsCenter, the first take. They're quite literally programmed to spread negativity. That negativity grabs your attention. When you see that negativity, you're naturally almost going to look. It's just some form of controversy. The fact that they're actually trying to spread negativity or trying to spark a narrative is just toxic. I have to try to find my ways to go off of that.

quotes.speaker: Breanna Stewart
quotes.summary_phrase: Breanna Stewart on detaching from public judgment
quotes.excerpt: If I'm not going to listen to you on advice about how to take care of my kids,
quotes.quote: I detach from judgment. If I'm not going to listen to you on advice about how to take care of my kids, you're not going to give me advice on how to play basketball or anything like that because you're not in that circle with me. Things are going to try to bring you down and you're the only one that can continue to stand tall.

quotes.speaker: Breanna Stewart
quotes.summary_phrase: Breanna Stewart's goal to leave the game better
quotes.excerpt: I want to leave everything better than I found it.
quotes.quote: I want to leave everything better than I found it. With the WNBA and the CBA and the way it's continuing to grow and change, that's most exciting. I plan on playing for the next however many years, but in 10 years from now, what's it going to be? I'm really honing in on my foundation and making sure I'm giving back to where I'm from, and that's Syracuse, New York. I want to make an impact beyond the basketball court.
